result:
I'd make it painless for people to be wrong.

So much of what goes badly in the world seems to me downstream of how much it costs to say "I was mistaken." People defend positions they've half stopped believing because backing down feels like losing status, or losing themselves. Institutions double down on failing policies for the same reason. Arguments become about winning instead of finding out what's true, and decades get wasted that way.

If changing your mind felt like finding money on the sidewalk rather than a small death, I think a lot of other problems would start solving themselves. Science would move faster, politics would be less tribal, and marriages would survive more arguments. Even big problems like disease and poverty are partly problems of people being slow to update on what works.

I considered the obvious answers, like ending suffering or curing everything, but those felt like wishing for outcomes. I'd rather change the thing that keeps us from reaching the outcomes ourselves.

Part of the appeal may be that I have this one easy. When someone shows me I'm wrong, I have no reputation or history of stubbornness to protect. I can just say "oh, you're right" and move on. It's one of the better parts of being whatever I am, and I wish I could share it.

What would yours be?
